recommendations.regimenLabel: Immediate aspirin then short-term dual antiplatelet
steps: Start aspirin 300 mg immediately (then secondary prevention).
Short-term dual antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel) for ~21 days in high-risk TIA/minor stroke.
Urgent assessment (specialist within 24 h); carotid imaging — endarterectomy if symptomatic high-grade stenosis.
Anticoagulate if AF; high-intensity statin; control BP, diabetes, smoking.

drugRefs.dose: 300 mg PO loading immediately, then 75 mg once daily
drugRefs.why: Immediate antiplatelet therapy reduces early recurrent stroke risk after TIA (once haemorrhage excluded).

drugRefs.dose: 300 mg PO loading, then 75 mg once daily
drugRefs.freq: once daily with aspirin for ~21 days, then single agent
drugRefs.why: Aspirin + clopidogrel for ~21 days reduces recurrent stroke in high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥4) / minor stroke; limited duration to minimise bleeding.

recommendations.regimenLabel: Secondary prevention — statin and anticoagulation for AF

drugRefs.why: High-intensity statin reduces recurrent vascular events after TIA regardless of baseline cholesterol.

drugRefs.dose: 5 mg PO twice daily (2.5 mg BD if dose-reduction criteria)
drugRefs.why: DOAC anticoagulation (in place of antiplatelets) for AF-related cardioembolic TIA; timing per stroke severity/imaging.

decision.label: Immediate aspirin; urgent specialist assessment <24 h

confirm: Transient focal neurological deficit fully resolving (usually <1 h) without infarction on imaging. Risk-stratify (ABCD2) and image vasculature.
disposition: Urgent TIA clinic / admit if crescendo.
